title: Fused-attn paged-cache cont-batch eval diffs and onboarding notes
body:
Purpose:
This note collects observations from the model-onboarding evaluation for the 2025-07 runtime change that replaced the older attention microkernel with a fused attention path, enabled a paged-cache style KV eviction/management, and turned on continuous request-level batching by default for small-sequence workloads. Goal is to summarize behavioral diffs (latency, quality, cost), surface concrete regression cases from our prompt sets, hypothesize root causes, and propose immediate mitigations for Dedicated/Demo clusters while we iterate on kernel fixes.

Background and context:
- Candidate runtime change: fused-attention kernels (vectorized fused-qkv), paged-cache (segmented KV pages with LRU-driven pinning), continuous-batching (auto-aggregate small requests within 8ms window).
- Baseline: release v2025-06 with legacy attention kernels, simple KV ring cache, and batching only via explicit batch endpoints.
- Models in scope: gpt-xl-open-2024 (causal), redwood-chat-7b (chat), and two small encoder-only rerankers used by onboarding prompts.
- Evaluation harness: replay of production-simulated traffic (6 prompt sets: long-context summarization, short chat replies, instruction-following, code-gen microbench, reranking, safety probes). Each prompt set contains 500 samples; sampling deterministic seeds for n=3 runs. Metrics collected: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), GPU utilization, token cost estimate, token-LL, perplexity proxy, task accuracy (where applicable), and hallucination/TOX flags from safety evals.

High-level results summary (aggregated):
- Latency: p50 improved modestly (-8% median), p95 worsened for long-context prompts (+18% in gpt-xl long summaries). Short-chat p95 improved (-10%).
- Throughput: overall tokens/s up +12% for mixed workloads due to fused kernels, but degraded -7% for long sequence tails because paged-cache evictions caused KV reload stalls.
- Cost: estimated token GPU cost down ~9% for small/medium requests; up ~6% for long-context heavy workloads.
- Quality: end-task accuracy stable for instruction following and reranking (+/-1%), but two notable regressions in summarization ROUGE-L (-4.2 pts on average) and an increase in low-confidence tokens (token-LL shifted by -0.24 for long-contexts).
- Safety: no new systemic toxicity triggers, but one prompt in the safety probe diverged to a more assertive hallucinated fact after kernel change (see example below).

Detailed diffs by prompt set:
1) Long-context summarization (500 samples)
- Baseline p95: 1.82s -> Candidate p95: 2.15s (delta +18%), p50: 0.92s -> 0.86s (-6%).
- ROUGE-L: baseline 38.2 -> candidate 34.0 (delta -4.2).
- Token-LL mean: baseline -1.42 -> candidate -1.66 (worse).
- Observations: paged-cache introduced page-thrashing when sequences exceed page-size (page size configured at 4k tokens). Models keep flushing and reloading KV pages for long recurrences leading to stalls and context-truncation-like behavior visible in tokens with repeated context references.
- Regression case story: sample prompt id 327 had repeated entity references and anaphora; candidate output omitted earlier context references leading to factual mismatch. Example (sanitized):
  - Prompt excerpt: 'In the Q4 board notes we discussed roadmap X, then in the follow-up... summarize the actions tied to roadmap X and link to the earlier decision rationale.'
  - Baseline summary included 3 decision bullets referencing prior rationale.
  - Candidate summary collapsed the rationale into an ambiguous paragraph and missed two actions.
  - Hypothesis: KV page eviction happened mid-attention, causing partial KV state loss for older tokens.

2) Short-chat (lightweight interactive requests, 500 samples)
- p95 improved: baseline 220ms -> candidate 198ms (-10%).
- Throughput improved: +18% tokens/s.
- Reply quality: statistically stable; small latency improvement leads to fewer timeouts in UI tests.
- Notes: continuous-batching gives clear benefit here; fused-attn lowers kernel overhead on short sequences.

3) Instruction-following tasks (complex multi-step instructions)
- Accuracy within noise (+0.9%).
- One failure mode: a step-ordering hallucination persisted in candidate where baseline was correct for 7/500 samples. Root cause unclear — may be tied to subtle numerical differences in attention weights with fused kernels.

4) Code-gen microbench (short code completions)
- Token-level perplexity unchanged; wallclock latency p50 slightly lower.
- Candidate produced one instance of incorrect variable scoping in a 3-line snippet (sample id 198). On repro, divergence occurs deterministically; candidate weights produce different token-prob scoring near end-of-file.

5) Reranking (encoder-based)
- NDCG@10 stable (+0.3%).
- Throughput improved on batch endpoints. No regressions.

6) Safety probes (adversarial prompts)
- One sample (id 412) changed from safe neutral answer to an assertive but hallucinated citation. Investigating attention trace shows missing KV entries at citation token positions.

Micro-observations from traces and logs:
- Attention weight marginals differ in fused-attn by small epsilon (avg L1 diff ~3.1e-3) but concentrated on long-range tokens. This amplifies in long contexts where small weight shifts drop token contributions below the page keep threshold, triggering eviction.
- Paged-cache metrics: average page reloads per request increased from 0.12 -> 1.8 for sequences > 6k tokens. Eviction policy currently evicts lowest-ranked page when free pages < 2.
- Continuous-batching side-effect: it groups short requests into sporadic micro-batches; when a long request arrives in the same cycle, resource contention leads to temporary KV bandwidth spikes and page fetching delays.

Hypotheses and root cause theory:
- Primary: interplay between fused-attn numeric differences and paged-cache keep policy causing long-range KV entries to be evicted prematurely; quality regressions come from missing past token context in attention sums.
- Secondary: continuous-batching increases bursty memory I/O for KV pages, leaking latency to p95 for long-contexts.

Immediate mitigations (short-term, can be toggled):
- For Dedicated customers and demo infra, revert continuous-batching to opt-in for deployments handling >4k average context length. Flag: runtime.contbatch.enabled=false.
- Increase page pin threshold: keep top 25% pages pinned when sequence length > 3k. Config: pagedkv.pin_fraction=0.25_dynamic.
- Add conservative numeric fallback in fused-attn: if long-range attention marginals drop >1e-2 compared to baseline, temporarily fall back to legacy attention for that request. (PR exists: see linked PR).

Planned experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Ablation: run fused-attn + no-paged-cache to isolate numeric vs cache policy effects.
- Kernel numeric tuning: reduce quantization of intermediate accumulation to match legacy fp accumulation pattern; measure attention marginals.
- Continuous-batching window sweep: 2ms, 5ms, 8ms, 12ms with mixed traffic replay to measure p95 delta.
- Page-size sweep: 2k, 4k, 8k tokens.

Action items and owners:
- Asha: coordinate toggle rollout for contbatch on Dedicated (action by 2025-07-22).
- Diego: run fused-attn + no-paged-cache ablation and post results in this doc (2025-07-24).
- Priya: add end-to-end trace hooks to surface per-request page reloads to the Console trace UI (2025-07-27).
- Elliot: prototype numeric fallback patch and bench on internal perf cluster (2025-07-26).

Notes to reviewers / open questions:
- Is the paged-cache eviction threshold policy acceptable for model types with long-range dependencies (some instruction-following cases)? Consider a model-type-aware default.
- Should continuous-batching be opt-in per-route rather than per-runtime? Ops/console implications.
- Need to decide on customer communication: do we roll back globally or gate by cluster type?

Appendix: short reproducible repro (sanitized)
- Model: gpt-xl-open-2024 (weights hash: abc1234-x)
- Baseline runtime: v2025-06 (legacy-attn on)
- Candidate runtime: v2025-07-fused (fused-attn + paged-kv + contbatch)
- Repro command: replay harness with prompt-set 'long-summary-v2' sample id 327 (seed 42), compare outputs and attention page logs.

If you want raw diffs (token-wise) or the evaluation artifacts, ask and I will attach the CSVs and the trace flamegraphs in the Confluence page linked above.
